document.title: Warhammer 40k Reforged Listbuilder - Catalogue Maintenance and Presentation Guide
document.supersedes: Catalogue Maintenance & Presentation Guide V2 and the standalone LISTBUILDER_UPDATE_WORKFLOW maintenance document
document.scope: This document explains how to audit, maintain, polish, and validate Reforged New Recruit catalogues. It is a procedural and presentation guide, not a semantic rules source and not a replacement for the Game System doctrine or army rules PDF.
document.intent: Future maintainers, including AI agents, should be able to use this document autonomously to understand what kind of work is being requested, which sources outrank others, how conservative a maintenance pass should be, what presentation problems to look for, and how to validate a change before returning it.
document.why_this_document_exists: This guide consolidates the project's active catalogue-maintenance procedures into one operational reference. The original Polish Pass Guide contributed presentation and review lessons; the former standalone Listbuilder Update Workflow contributed rules-version update procedure, baseline-only update handling, Patch Notes maintenance, compatibility-only Game System sync, and patch-cycle completion checks. Durable semantic and engine doctrine remains in the Game System. Historical faction-by-faction snapshots and duplicated maintenance instructions are intentionally excluded from this active guide.
how_to_use_this_document: Read the current Game System first when the task may affect semantics, shared categories, Game Size, Leader Capacity, attachments, Additional Copy Costs, shared libraries, IDs, or New Recruit runtime conventions.
Read the authoritative army rules PDF for player-facing rules text, unit legality, points, loadouts, attachments, and faction-specific semantics.
Treat the current executable catalogue and observed New Recruit runtime behavior as authoritative for what is actually implemented; stale comments and historical notes do not override live behavior.
Use this guide to structure the audit, presentation review, implementation discipline, and validation process.

For routine rules-version updates, the maintainer should normally need to provide only the catalogue/faction, the new army-rules version, and the listbuilding-relevant changes they know about. Treat version metadata, Patch Notes maintenance, Game System compatibility checks, linked-library synchronization, and validation as normal autonomous maintenance work unless the user says otherwise.

When the requested work is a normal maintenance pass, propose genuinely nontrivial mechanical changes before implementing them. Straightforward presentation cleanup and already-established patterns may be applied directly.
Do not silently broaden the task. Preserve stable mechanics that are outside the approved scope.
authority_order: Authoritative army rules PDF for source rules and player-facing wording.
Current Game System for reusable listbuilder doctrine and proven New Recruit implementation standards.
Current executable catalogue and linked libraries for deployed implementation state.
Observed New Recruit runtime behavior for engine reality.
This guide for maintenance process, presentation review, and validation discipline.
Historical comments and archived revision notes for archaeology only.

maintenance_philosophy.core_goal: Make the catalogue faster to scan, easier to record correctly, and harder to misuse without turning presentation cleanup into a rules rewrite.
presentation_priority_questions: Which model or model-group does this choice belong to?
What is that model or group equipped with?
maintenance_philosophy.standardisation_rule: Standardise the visual grammar and naming conventions, but do not force unlike rules into identical shapes. Preserve unit-specific distinctions when they help the player understand the actual choice.
conservative_change_policy: Prefer labels, wrappers, ordering, grouping, direct checkbox conversions, and comment cleanup during a normal maintenance pass.
Do not redesign a functioning mechanical structure merely because it looks unconventional in JSON.
Change mechanics when the current implementation is actually wrong, causes a player-facing problem, violates current source semantics, or the user explicitly approves the redesign.
Do not remove an odd-looking structure until you understand what problem it is solving.
Runtime-test unfamiliar or engine-sensitive structures instead of assuming BattleScribe/New Recruit behavior.
semantic_guardrails: Never invent game semantics to make New Recruit easier.
Never silently change points, eligibility, attachment legality, copy-cost arithmetic, ratios, Rare behavior, or hidden semantic categories during presentation-only work.
Never conditionally hide an option after it has already been selected.
Prefer visible final-state choices over procedural replacement steps.
Do not expose raw New Recruit implementation vocabulary to players.

model_identity: Use explicit model or model-group headers when they materially improve readability.
Use the real role/model noun when the source establishes one.
Do not invent a canonical noun merely to avoid a generic fallback.
Anonymous choice lists are acceptable only when their ownership is already obvious.
section_names: Use Loadout Options for ordinary equipment decisions.
Use Paid Wargear for additive purchased equipment.
Use Unit Upgrade, Mutation Upgrade, Protocol Upgrade, or another specific semantic heading for abstract state purchases.
Use Additional Model for a max-one optional model.
Use Attached [MODEL/LEADER] for nested player-facing relationships.
Do not use Special Weapon Loadouts merely as catalogue taxonomy.
Do not use generic Additional Leader when the actual attached model has a meaningful identity.

retain_when: The slot explains a real dependency.
The physical position is itself a meaningful choice.
The label describes a useful equipment category such as Main Weapon, Coaxial Weapon, or Sidearm.
physical_slot_labels.principle: Do not narrate implementation slots unless the slot identity helps the player understand the rule.

atomic_packages.rule: Use ' & ' for inseparable final-state equipment packages.
atomic_packages.avoid: Do not use '+' for atomic packages.
atomic_packages.meaningful_choice_first: Where several packages share the same component, put the differentiating component first if doing so improves scanability. Do not mechanically reorder every package.

fixed_vs_choice_components.rule: If one component is always present and another is the real choice, split the fixed component into its own visible line when doing so is mechanically safe.
fixed_vs_choice_components.warning: Do not split the package when a branch replaces the whole package and the split would require brittle conditional mandatory groups, selected-hidden behavior, fake No Weapon states, or other implementation complexity.

relationship_ordering: A genuine Leader-like relationship may appear before Loadout Options when it is a primary roster decision.
A wargear-like attached model may appear after Loadout Options or Additional Model.
Apply individual consideration rather than a universal ordering rule.
micro_consistency: Keep established weapon spelling and spacing consistent with current source authority.
Do not 'correct' source-derived player-facing rule text merely for stylistic consistency.

new_recruit_review_hazards: Selected-hidden entries are invalid. Never design a flow where a selected option later becomes hidden.
Dynamically revealed mandatory/default child selectors may not instantiate their default reliably. Runtime-test them.
Nested units can be valid Association targets.
Candidate-side association-count invalidation has behaved badly for host exclusivity. Prefer host-owned constructive validation.
Direct optional upgrades with max 1 are the proven checkbox pattern for one-off additive wargear.
For optional model checkboxes, retain the useful structural wrapper and place max 1 on the direct type:model child.
Optional max-1 radio groups with no minimum/default may expose a visible empty radio state.
Zero-width group labels may suppress redundant headers while preserving structural semantics.
Local entryLink display names may not control exported names; New Recruit may use the shared target's canonical name.
A separate accounting Configuration may not see association counts reliably; only use a selection-count proxy where source semantics guarantee the mapping.

catalogue_maintenance_workflow.name: Establish the baseline
actions: Record catalogue name, revision, Game System revision, catalogue ID, and linked-library IDs/revisions.
Confirm the authoritative rules PDF/version the catalogue is meant to represent.
Snapshot existing IDs before editing.
Identify known deferred work and intentional exceptions.

catalogue_maintenance_workflow.name: Audit the shell
actions: List root units, shared units, linked-library imports, and Configuration entries.
Inspect top-level group headings and repeated presentation patterns.
Find stale terminology, anonymous groups, implementation-facing slot labels, old '+' atomic packages, and stale comments.
Check whether player-facing rules contradict executable behavior.

catalogue_maintenance_workflow.name: Classify each finding
actions: Presentation-only cleanup.
Comment/documentation cleanup.
Live implementation bug.
Source-version mismatch.
Potential mechanical redesign.
Known deferred issue.
Intentional exception.

catalogue_maintenance_workflow.name: Choose the change boundary
actions: Apply established presentation patterns directly when the semantics are already clear.
Discuss genuinely weird or nontrivial mechanical changes before implementing them.
Do not broaden a presentation pass into unrelated rules work.
For shared libraries, determine whether the change is intrinsic to the reusable unit tree or consumer-local.

catalogue_maintenance_workflow.name: Implement conservatively
actions: Preserve existing live IDs.
Use deterministic IDs only for genuinely new objects.
Preserve points, defaults, modifiers, conditions, category links, info links, constraints, associations, and sort semantics unless they are part of the approved change.
Prefer the simplest exact representation over clever abstraction.
Keep source-derived rule descriptions verbatim unless the authoritative source itself changed.

catalogue_maintenance_workflow.name: Validate aggressively
actions: Parse the output JSON again.
Check duplicate IDs.
Compare ID sets and identify every addition/removal intentionally.
Verify no unexpected rule descriptions changed.
Verify linked-library target IDs, display labels, importRootEntries, and shared-root sync where relevant.
Verify Additional Copy Cost arithmetic and hidden semantic markers if touched.
Verify attachment eligibility and constructive errors if touched.
Runtime-test unfamiliar New Recruit structures.
For a rules-version update, confirm every requested points/loadout/list-construction change is present and no battlefield-only change leaked into the catalogue.
For compatibility-only Game System syncs, normalize the changed metadata and confirm the remaining object is equivalent to the source.

catalogue_maintenance_workflow.name: Record the maintenance result
actions: Bump revision for executable/player-visible changes.
Do not bump solely for comment-only cleanup unless project policy specifically requires it.
Update Catalogue Bugfixes only for bugs/misimplementations that actually went live.
Do not log corrections to unreleased WIP as player-facing bugfixes.
Retain cumulative live bugfix entries unless the underlying correction is genuinely reverted.
Use a concise maintenance fingerprint when appropriate.
Consolidate stale comments into current state, authoring/runtime notes, and concise history.

principles: Complete reusable unit trees belong in the shared library; consumers should use thin entryLinks.
The library owns intrinsic unit-tree content.
The consumer owns host-specific availability, presentation, Configuration gating, consumer-local eligibility/attachment semantics, and catalogue-local accounting.
Do not update a shared library for a consumer-local change.
If a portable shared root gains intrinsic executable validation that depends on a hidden semantic category, sync both the root and that category into the shared library.
Verify the actual linked library before changing human-readable catalogueLink labels.
Do not assume a local entryLink name controls exported text.
When a portable/shared unit changes intrinsically, synchronize all owned copies or the shared-library source in the same maintenance pass.
Preserve stable shared target IDs so existing consumer catalogues continue resolving the same reusable unit identity.
Do not rebuild or rewrite an unchanged linked library merely to keep human-readable version labels cosmetically synchronized.
sync_check: Confirm source and library versions before copying.
Compare the intended shared root structurally after sync.
Confirm all required hidden categories or shared dependencies exist in the library.
Confirm unrelated shared roots are unchanged.

reviewer_questions: Can the player tell which model this choice belongs to at a glance?
Is this label describing a real player decision, or only how the JSON happens to be implemented?
If several options share the same component, would putting the meaningful difference first make them easier to scan?
Is a fixed component being repeated unnecessarily?
Would flattening this wrapper make the unit easier to scan without changing mechanics?
Is this truly Paid Wargear, or an abstract Unit Upgrade?
Does this error follow the three-part corrective pattern when permissive-corrective validation is appropriate?
Am I trying to solve a presentation problem by changing mechanics?
Is this odd structure solving a real New Recruit behavior problem?
Is this an intentional exception that should be documented instead of homogenised?
If this unit is shared, does the change belong in the reusable unit tree or only in this consumer?
Would the player understand the exported roster without seeing the editor structure that produced it?

autonomous_ai_operating_notes.default_behavior: Treat a catalogue-maintenance request as an audit first unless the user explicitly asks for immediate implementation. Report the current state, identify live bugs separately from presentation opportunities, and distinguish safe established cleanups from changes that need discussion.
when_to_implement_without_further_confir: The user explicitly says to implement/apply/fix the proposed slate.
The change is a straightforward application of a previously proven project pattern and the user has already approved that class of change.
The change is comments/documentation cleanup that does not alter semantics or player-visible behavior.
when_to_stop_and_discuss: A change would alter points, eligibility, attachment legality, copy-cost arithmetic, ratios, or unit identity.
A proposed structure depends on unproven New Recruit behavior.
A shared-library change could affect multiple consumers.
Two current sources disagree and executable behavior does not resolve the conflict.
autonomous_ai_operating_notes.output_expectation: Return a clearly named revised artifact, summarize exactly what changed and what was intentionally preserved, and recommend targeted runtime tests only where New Recruit behavior is not already proven.

historical_note.original_document: Listbuilder Polish Pass Guide v1, generated 2026-08-28
historical_note.archival_status: The original document remains useful as project archaeology because it records the early cross-faction Polish Pass and faction-by-faction results. Those historical revision snapshots are intentionally omitted from this active V2 guide so they cannot be mistaken for current project state.
historical_note.v3_migration: V3 absorbs the surviving operational content of the former standalone LISTBUILDER_UPDATE_WORKFLOW: the minimal update contract, narrow rules-version update procedure, cumulative Patch Notes rules, baseline-only updates, compatibility-only Game System validation, shared-unit synchronization, and final patch-cycle sweep. The remainder of that document was intentionally retired as duplication.

rules_version_update_workflow.scope: Use this workflow when an existing healthy catalogue is moving to a newer army-rules publication. This is narrower than a general catalogue audit: preserve existing working architecture and implement only changes relevant to list construction.

maintainer_normally_provides: Listbuilding-relevant changes known to the maintainer.
minimal_update_contract.autonomous_maintenance_expectation: Everything else in this workflow is normal maintenance work and should be handled automatically unless the maintainer explicitly narrows the task.

procedure: Start from the latest healthy executable catalogue, not an older rules PDF, stale catalogue copy, or experimental branch.
Treat the supplied army-rules version as the new catalogue baseline.
Implement only changes that affect list construction. Do not reproduce battlefield-only rules changes and do not invent builder changes merely because a datasheet changed.
Preserve stable IDs for semantic objects that still exist. Rename or retune the existing object when appropriate; create deterministic IDs only for genuinely new objects.

Preserve existing catalogue mechanics unless the rules update actually changes them. This includes presentation categories, attachments, validation, Additional Copy Cost arithmetic, Game Size logic, Configuration behavior, and compatibility structures.
Update catalogue version metadata and increment the catalogue revision for the new release baseline.
Update Patch Notes with builder-relevant army changes only.
Keep the catalogue pointed at the current Game System revision. Treat the rules-version update as an opportunity to catch stale Game System targets without altering Game System mechanics.
When an intrinsic portable/shared unit changes, synchronize every owned copy or shared-library source in the same pass while preserving stable target IDs.
If a linked library's mechanics did not change, do not rebuild it merely because the consumer catalogue received a new rules version.

patch_notes_maintenance.scope: Applies whenever a catalogue uses the standard player-facing Patch Notes Configuration.
rules: Patch Notes contain only army changes relevant to list construction.
Do not repeat a change already implemented in an earlier catalogue revision merely because a later rules publication makes it official.
Catalogue Bugfixes are cumulative. Keep previous still-live bugfix bullets, update the Catalogue Bugfixes date to the current work date, and append newly confirmed live bugfixes.
Remove an older bugfix bullet only when that specific correction has genuinely been reverted and is no longer true.
Do not reset, replace, or prune cumulative bugfix history merely because a new work session, revision, or publication date has started.
Do not record corrections to unreleased WIP as player-facing Catalogue Bugfixes.
Retain the standard Reforged Discord reference whenever Patch Notes are present.

baseline_only_rules_update.scope: Use this when a faction receives a new army-rules version but there are no listbuilder-relevant mechanical changes.
procedure: Update the catalogue's rules-version name.
Increment the catalogue revision.
Update the Patch Notes publication baseline.
Retain the cumulative Catalogue Bugfixes section.
Point the catalogue at the current Game System revision.
Make no mechanical catalogue changes.
baseline_only_rules_update.validation: A baseline-only update should differ only in the intended version/revision/Patch Notes/Game System metadata. Normalize those intentional metadata changes back to the source values and confirm the resulting object is otherwise equivalent.

patch_cycle_completion_sweep.scope: Run after a batch of army-rules updates or a Game System revision rollout is complete.
procedure: Audit the active executable catalogue set and owned shared libraries for stale Game System revision targets.
Retarget any remaining live catalogue or owned library to the current Game System revision in a strict compatibility-only pass.
Do not alter catalogue mechanics during the compatibility sync.
After normalizing the intended Game System metadata difference back to the source value, confirm the resulting object is otherwise equivalent.
